title: Volcano

evidence.note: Wikipedia's article on the 17-cartoon Superman series says all entries are in the US public domain because National failed to renew their copyrights. That is a secondary claim. A partial read of the Catalog of Copyright Entries 1969-1971 motion picture renewal volumes found no Volcano or Superman renewal. The Jul-Dec 1969 renewals and the S and V sections of Jul-Dec 1970 were not read, so absence is not confirmed.
evidence.source: Catalog of Copyright Entries, Motion Pictures, 1970 renewals (partial read)

evidence.note: Sound film with music credited to Sammy Timberg. The recorded track would normally share the print's status, which is unresolved.
Based on the DC Comics character Superman. The character's own copyright status was not checked here. The series article says rights to the cartoons reverted to National Comics.
Superman is a DC character and franchise. The series article says Warner Bros. owns the ancillary rights and the original 35 mm master elements. Character marks survive copyright expiry.

Warner Bros. Home Entertainment issued a 2023 Blu-ray set of all 17 cartoons, taken from high-definition restorations of the original 35 mm elements. A faithful restoration adds no new copyright. Added material, if any, was not verified.

editorial:
Volcano is the eighth of 17 Technicolor Superman shorts from Fleischer Studios. Dave Fleischer directed, and Paramount released it on July 10, 1942. Sammy Timberg is credited with the music. A Superman cartoon like this is a ready-made clip for superhero history, animation studies or retro-style projects.

The trap is that the cartoon is not one clean right. Wikipedia reports that the series fell into the public domain because National never renewed, but I could not confirm that from the catalog volumes. Superman is also a live DC character and franchise, and Warner Bros. holds the original 35 mm elements and issued the 2023 Blu-ray. Use an older circulating copy, not the Warner restoration, and keep out of any use that implies a DC or Warner link.
faq: Is the 1942 Superman cartoon Volcano free to reuse?

The film print is reported to be public domain, but I could not verify the renewal absence from primary records. Check the Copyright Office and catalog volumes yourself before relying on it. Superman as a trademark is still held by DC and Warner.
Can I use the 2023 Warner Blu-ray transfer?

A faithful restoration adds no new US copyright, but the disc is copy-protected. Ripping it can violate 17 U.S.C. 1201. Added material, if any, may be protected. An older Internet Archive copy avoids both issues.
